propositions.text: The claimant and family members, Hungarian citizens, seek refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXXX XXXXX and his spouse, XXXXX XXXXX, and their minor children, XXXXX XXXXX and XXXXX XXXXX, their adult son XXXXX XXXXX (Jr.) and his common-law spouse, XXXXX XXXXX, and the claimant's spouse's father (claimant's father-in-law) XXXXX XXXXX, citizens of Hungary, seek refugee protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act1 (the IRPA).

propositions.text: Claimants' identities established through certified copies of passports.
propositions.quote: The claimants' identities have been established through certified copies of the claimants' passports.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant and family, Hungarian citizens, seek refugee protection under IRPA; their identities are established by passports, says the court.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges discrimination, harassment, and harm in Hungary due to Roma race, affecting employment, education, housing, and public life.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that as a Roma in Hungary he will be discriminated against, harassed and even harmed simply because of his race. The discrimination is felt on many levels including in employment, education, housing, and in the general public.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges racial discrimination and harm as a Roma in Hungary in many life areas, says the claimant.

propositions.text: Claimant and family were victims of threats, attacks, sexual advances, death threats, and school discrimination.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges he and his other family members were victims of verbal threats, physical attacks, inappropriate sexual advances, death threats, and discrimination in school.

propositions.text: Claimant fled to Canada on April 24, 2009 and made refugee claim same day; son, daughter-in-law, and father-in-law made subsequent claims.
propositions.quote: The claimant fled to Canada on April 24, 2009 and made a claim for refugee protection that same day. The claimant's son and daughter-in-law and his father-in-law arrived in Canada and made their own claims for refugee claims subsequent to the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges family suffered threats and attacks; fled to Canada in 2009 and family made subsequent claims, says the claimant.

propositions.text: Claimant is designated representative of his minor children.
propositions.quote: The claimant is the designated representative of his minor children.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is the designated representative of his minor children, says the court.

propositions.text: Claimant failed to establish serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture, life risk, or cruel treatment on return to Hungary.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant has not satisfied the burden of establishing a serious possibility of persecution for a Convention ground, or that he would personally be subjected, on a balance of probabilities, to a danger of torture, or a risk to life or a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment upon return to his country.

propositions.text: Claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: Therefore, I find that the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed to prove persecution or risk and is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The key issue is whether the claimant's fear is objectively reasonable, considering state protection adequacy and claimant's efforts to seek it.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue in this case is whether the claimant's fear is objectively reasonable. In this regard, I considered whether or not there is adequate state protection in Hungary, whether the claimant took all reasonable steps to avail himself of that protection, and whether he has provided clear and convincing evidence of the state's inability to protect.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the key issue is whether claimant's fear is objectively reasonable, considering state protection and claimant's efforts.

propositions.text: At June 2, 2011 hearing, claimants could not swear PIFs were true due to lack of contact with former counsel and interpreter.
propositions.quote: At the previous hearing, which was held on June 2, 2011, the claimants testified that they could not swear that the Personal Information Forms (PIF) were complete true and correct, because they had not met with the former counsel or his interpreter and could not verify what was contained in the narratives.

propositions.text: Claimants alleged misconduct by former counsel but did not make formal complaint to governing body.
propositions.quote: The claimants obtained new counsel and alleged misconduct on the part of former counsel. I explained to the claimants that I could not accept allegations against former counsel without that counsel being given an opportunity to respond to the allegations. I told the claimants I would consider their explanation for not swearing to the PIF's if they made a formal complaint against the governing body former counsel belongs to, but the claimants decided for their own reasons not to make a complaint.

propositions.text: Claimants were instructed to provide revised narrative 20 days before next hearing but failed to do so by September 15, 2011.
propositions.quote: Additionally, the claimants were instructed to provide a revised narrative 20 days prior to the next hearing. At the resumption of the hearing on September 15, 2011, the claimants failed to do so.

propositions.text: Claimant gave no explanation for failure to provide updated narrative; interpreter unable to make appointments with claimants.
propositions.quote: I asked the claimant why this was not done. The claimant testified he did not know why he did not do so. Counsel submits that his interpreter tried to make appointments with the claimants, but was unable to do so.

propositions.text: Claimant's failure to provide updated narrative undermines credibility.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant failed to provide a reasonable explanation for not providing an updated narrative to the Board since he was given approximately 3 months to do so. This undermines the claimant's credibility.

propositions.text: PIFs given no weight as claimants would not swear they were complete, true and correct.
propositions.quote: I give the claimants PIF's which were submitted to the Board no weight, since the claimants would not swear that the PIF's were complete, true and correct.

propositions.text: Since narratives unreliable and claimants ready to proceed, oral testimonies considered.
propositions.quote: Therefore, since I could not rely on the information contained in the narratives, and the claimants indicated they were ready to proceed, I considered the claimants; oral testimonies.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found claimants did not swear PIFs, failed to provide updated narrative, undermining credibility; relied on oral testimony.

propositions.text: Roma are Hungary's largest ethnic minority, estimated between 200,000 and 800,000 persons, facing discrimination and violence in many life areas.
propositions.quote: According to the Central Statistics Office, in 2007 the Romani community was the largest ethnic minority, accounting for 2% of the population, or about 200,000 persons. However, unofficial estimates, which vary widely, suggest the actual figure was much higher, ranging between 500,000 and 800,000 persons. Violent attacks against Roma continued and generated strong public concern and intense disputes as to the existence of racially motivated crime in the country. Human rights NGO's reported that Roma were discriminated against in almost all fields of life, particularly in employment, education, housing, penal institutions, and access to public places, such as restaurants and bars. According to statistics of the Hungarian Institute for Educational Research and Development, Roma were significantly less educated than other citizens, and their incomes and life expectancy were well below average. A 2007 International Labor Organization report estimated the unemployment rate among Roma to be 40%. However, in many underdeveloped regions of the country, it exceeded 90%. Romani unemployment was estimated to be 3 to 5 times higher than among the non-Romani population. Inadequate housing continued to be a problem for Roma; their overall living conditions remained significantly worse than the general population's.3 The attitude of some of Hungarian people, including some in positions of authority, toward the Roma is certainly discriminatory and prejudicial. It is clear from the documentary evidence that the effect has been to marginalize the Roma people. Roma are generally under-employed, under-educated, frequently live in subsistence housing, and are now subject to violence from radical elements who are gaining support from the general public to some extent. It is against this background, and in taking into consideration the particular circumstances relating to this claim, that I must determine whether or not adequate state protection exists for this particular claimant in Hungary.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Roma are Hungary's largest minority, facing widespread discrimination, poor living conditions, and violence, setting context for state protection analysis.

propositions.text: There is a presumption that countries can protect citizens; refugee protection applies only when no other recourse exists.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue in the case at hand is the presumption that countries are capable of protecting its citizens, and this underscores the principle that international protection comes into play only when a refugee claimant has no other recourse available.

propositions.text: Board is not obliged to prove Hungary can protect; applicant bears burden to rebut presumption of adequate state protection with clear and convincing evidence on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: The Board is not obliged to prove that Hungary can offer the Applicant effective state protection, rather, the Applicant bears the legal burden of rebutting the presumption that adequate state protection exists by adducing clear and convincing evidence which satisfies the Board on a balance of probabilities.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the presumption that countries protect citizens; applicant must rebut this with clear, convincing evidence on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: To rebut presumption of state protection, claimant must provide clear and convincing evidence of state's inability to protect on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: In other words, to rebut the presumption of state protection, a claimant must provide "clear and convincing" confirmation of the state's inability to protect its citizens.

propositions.text: Evidence of inadequate state protection must be reliable, probative, and satisfy Board on balance of probabilities.
propositions.quote: A claimant who alleges that state protection is inadequate must persuade the Board that the evidence establishes that the state protection is in fact, inadequate. The evidence that state protection is inadequate must not only be reliable and probative, it must also satisfy the Board, on a balance of probabilities, that state protection is inadequate.

propositions.text: Claimant must show all reasonable steps taken to seek protection, considering country context and claimant's interactions with authorities.
propositions.quote: A claimant must show that they have taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek protection, taking into account the context of the country of origin, the steps taken and the claimant's interactions with the authorities.

propositions.text: Claimant testified about 2006 attack and police response; police told him to identify assailants but he could not.
propositions.quote: I considered whether or not the claimant took all reasonable steps in his circumstances to seek protection. The claimant testified that in 2006, he went to have a beer with a friend and that he was attacked by people who asked him what a gypsy was doing there. The claimant testified he went to the police and they told him if he was able to recognize his assailants, he should tell the police. The claimant was asked if he recognized the assailants. The claimant testified he did not know.

propositions.text: Claimant did not provide enough information for police to investigate; presumption of adequate state protection not rebutted in this case.
propositions.quote: Since the claimant was unable to provide a description of the assailants to the police, I find that the police were not given enough information to conduct a proper investigation, so in the circumstances in this particular case, the claimant has not rebutted the presumption that adequate state protection exists in Hungary.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains claimant must provide clear evidence of inadequate state protection and shows claimant failed to provide enough info to police, so presumption not rebutted.

propositions.text: Claimant testified horses stolen in 2009; police told him to report if he recognized location; claimant did not follow up and fled to Canada.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified regarding an incident in 2009 in which eight people stole his two horses. The claimant testified he went to the police, who told him if he recognized where his horses were, to let them know. The claimant testified he did not follow up with the police again, because shortly afterwards, he fled to Canada.

propositions.text: Federal Court held fleeing before police investigation does not mean lack of state protection.
propositions.quote: The Federal Court has held that a claimant's decision to flee before police have had an opportunity to properly respond to and investigate a transgression did not amount to a lack of state protection.

propositions.text: No evidence police failed to investigate claimant's allegations; claimant's fleeing may have delayed investigation.
propositions.quote: In this particular case, there is no information to suggest that police were not making genuine and earnest efforts to investigate the claimant's allegations and apprehend the claimant's perpetrator. The claimant's choice to leave Hungary may have resulted in the investigation being delayed or stymied, given that he, as the victim, was a key witness.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's fleeing before police follow-up does not prove lack of state protection; no evidence police failed to investigate.

propositions.text: Claimant testified daughter was victim of unwanted sexual advances by police officer; conflicting testimony about reporting to police.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified that his daughter was the victim of unwanted sexual advancements by a police officer. The claimant testified he did not report this to the police, because in his view, the police would consider that nothing happened. The claimant went on to say his daughter reported this to the police, but they sent her away.

propositions.text: Claimant gave inconsistent testimony about police reporting; court draws negative inference on credibility.
propositions.quote: I asked the claimant why he gave what appeared to be two different answers. The claimant testified he did not go to the police, but his daughter did. I draw a negative inference relating to the credibility in this instance because of the inconsistency in his testimony, and that it doesn't make sense his daughter would report to this to the police if by his own testimony there was not sense in reporting it.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes claimant's inconsistent testimony about daughter's police report and draws negative credibility inference.

propositions.text: Claimant did not provide clear and convincing evidence of taking all reasonable steps to seek state protection before seeking international protection.
propositions.quote: Each of the adult claimants described other particular incidents which they experienced themselves, but in relation to the principal claimant's testimony, I find that he has not provided the requisite clear and convincing evidence that they took all reasonable steps to seek state protection in their own country before seeking international protection.

propositions.text: Claimant could not identify assailants and fled Canada without police follow-up; these vague accounts fall short of clear evidence of inadequate state protection.
propositions.quote: In the first instance, the claimant could not identify the assailants. In the second incident, in which his horses were stolen, he fled Canada and did not follow up with the police in relation to his complaint. These two unsubstantiated and vague accounts that he went to the police falls short of the clear and convincing evidence that is need to determine on a balance of probabilities state protection in Hungary is inadequate.

propositions.text: Claimant did not take all reasonable steps to seek state protection before leaving Hungary; presumption of adequate state protection not rebutted.
propositions.quote: The claimant did not take all reasonable steps to seek state protection before leaving Hungary, so the presumption that there is adequate state protection in Hungary is not rebutted.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant failed to show clear evidence of seeking state protection; presumption of adequate protection not rebutted.

propositions.text: Claimant's views on state protection were not credible, unsubstantiated, and inconsistent with documentary evidence.
propositions.quote: I found the claimant's responses regarding the effectiveness of state protection were not persuasive, since they were not credible and were largely unsubstantiated and were not consistent with the documentary evidence.

propositions.text: Court prefers documentary evidence over claimant's testimony as it is from reliable, public sources.
propositions.quote: I prefer the documentary evidence over the claimants' testimony since they are drawn from a wide range of publically accessible documents, from reliable nongovernment and government organizations.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's views on state protection not credible and prefers reliable documentary evidence over testimony.

propositions.text: Counsel submits Hungary's legislation and policies have not translated into meaningful protection of Roma; cites reports on justice system shortcomings.
propositions.quote: Counsel submits that while Hungary is a democratic state and that the government has given verbal commitments that they are trying to tackle problems relating to the treatment of Roma, in actual fact, the legislation and the policies have not translated into meaningful protection of the Roma. Counsel submits numerous reports9 to demonstrate the shortcomings of the Hungarian justice system relating to the situation of the Roma. Counsel submits that Amnesty International reports that the failure to record, investigate and prosecute and punish racially-motivated crimes and provide remedies to the victims is letting down the Roma community.

propositions.text: Court agrees criticism of Hungarian government by NGOs is warranted but counsel has not shown state protection is so inadequate that claimants could not seek it.
propositions.quote: I do not take issue with counsel's submissions in this particular regard. In my view, criticism of the Hungarian government by NGO's is warranted, since the problems relating to the Roma are ongoing. However, even though the situation in Hungary is far from perfect, counsel by way of submissions has not demonstrated that state protection in Hungary is so inadequate, it would have been unreasonable for the claimants to have sought state protection.

propositions.text: Claimants failed first step of state protection analysis by not taking all reasonable steps to seek protection before seeking Canadian protection.
propositions.quote: That is not the case, and as I have already found, the claimants failed the first step in the analysis relating to state protection - they didn't first take all reasonable steps to seek that protection in their home country before seeking protection in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits Hungary's policies fail Roma protection; court agrees but finds claimants failed to seek state protection first.

propositions.text: Counsel submits rise of far-right Jobbik party shows increased racism and scapegoating of Roma in Hungary.
propositions.quote: Counsel submits that the rise of the right-wing extremist party, the Jobbik, who gained 17% of the vote in the last federal election, is an indication that in post-communist Europe, the old-fashioned far-right still finds scapegoats and equates the difficult economic times with the rise against Roma in Hungary.

propositions.text: Court shares concerns about far-right extremism and racism but finds Hungary acknowledges problems and is making serious efforts to protect minorities including Roma.
propositions.quote: As a decision maker in this case, I have similar concerns as counsel relating to far-right extremism and the rise of racism in Hungary. I would be remiss if I did not acknowledge and consider that there is information in the documentation to indicate that there is widespread reporting of incidents of intolerance, discrimination and persecution of Romani individuals in Hungary. However, weighted against this is persuasive evidence that indicates that Hungary candidly acknowledges its problems and is making serious efforts to rectify the treatment of minorities in that country, especially in the case of the Roma.

propositions.text: Despite some inconsistencies, objective evidence shows Hungary provides adequate state protection for Roma victims of crime and discrimination and is willing and able to protect them.
propositions.quote: The Board recognizes that there are some inconsistencies among several sources within the documentary evidence; however, the preponderance of the objective evidence regarding current country conditions suggests that, although not perfect, there is an adequate state protection in Hungary for Roma who are victims of crime, police abuse, discrimination or persecution, that Hungary is making serious efforts to address these problems, and that the police and government officials are both willing and able to protect victims.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits rise of far-right party shows racism; court acknowledges concerns but finds Hungary provides adequate state protection for Roma.

propositions.text: Hungary adopted legislation in 1993 guaranteeing minority rights and prohibiting ethnic discrimination; minorities have local representation and cultural rights.
propositions.quote: There is in considerable activism in Hungary by the country's ethnic minorities for the protection of their rights. In July 1993 the government adopted legislation guaranteeing the cultural, civil and political rights of 12 minority groups and prohibiting ethnic discrimination. Following the approval of this legislation, minority rights activists launched a new campaign to change Hungary's electoral law, with the aim of securing the direct representation of ethnic groups in the legislature. In the 1994 municipal elections, ethnic minorities were able to elect their own local ethnic authorities, with consultative roles on cultural and educational issues affecting the community. In February 1995 Hungary signed the counsel of Europe Convention on the Protection of National Minorities. In April the role of Hungary elected their own governing body, the National Autonomous Authority of the Romany minority, which was in power to administer funds and deliberate issues affecting the Roma. In December 2008 the Metropolitan Court in Budapest ordered the dissolution of the extreme nationalist Hungarian Guard, which was responsible for attacks and discriminatory behaviour against the Roma community. A court of appeal upheld the ruling, stating that the organization incited violence and violated the freedom of others. This prohibition was confirmed by the Supreme Court in December, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Hungary has enacted laws and measures since 1993 to protect minority rights and dissolved extremist groups attacking Roma.

propositions.text: Roma have minority self-governments organizing cultural and educational affairs with rights to participate in local government assemblies.
propositions.quote: Roma, like the other 12 official minorities, are entitled to elect their own minority self-government's (MSGs), which organized minority activities and handle cultural and educational affairs. The president of each MSG also has the right to attend and speak at local government assemblies.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Roma have minority self-governments managing cultural affairs and participating in local government.

propositions.text: Reports show police corruption and excessive force against Roma but state takes action when complaints made; Independent Police Complaints Board (IPCB) established in 2008.
propositions.quote: While there are reports of police corruption, and that police sometimes use excessive force against Roma, the evidence12 also shows that the state takes action when complaints are made. Sources indicate that the Independent Police Complaints Board (IPCB) began operation in January 2008. The IPCB, which is independent of the police, reviews complaints of police actions which violate fundamental rights and makes recommendations to the head of the National Police. If the recommendations are not accepted, the matter can be referred to a court. The Budapest-based NGO European Roma Rights Center (ERRC) describes the IPCB as a credible and independent watchdog to ensure the accountability of the police and has called for the government to ensure the IPCB's independence and strengthen its mandate. However, it is to be noted that there is criticism that the police followed up on only a small proportion of the IPCB's recommendations.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds police corruption and excessive force reports but notes state action via IPCB, an independent police complaints body since 2008.

propositions.text: In 10 months, authorities disciplined thousands of police officers; IPCB reviewed complaints and found violations but police often rejected recommendations.
propositions.quote: Further documentary evidence indicates: In the first 10 months of the year, authorities found 2,914 police officers responsible for breaches of discipline, 868 guilty of petty offenses, 310 guilty of criminal offenses, and eight unfit for duty. In the same period, courts sentenced seven police officers to prison terms, gave suspended sentences to 25, fined 315, demoted four, and dismissed 11. In the same period courts convicted 32 officers of corruption. No information was available on the number placed on probation. The IPCB, established in 2008, investigated violations and omissions by the police that affected fundamental rights. The five-member body, appointed by a two-thirds majority of the National Assembly, functions independently of police authorities. As of December 8, the board had received 285 complaints from the public. It reviewed 501 (including some cases filed in 2009) and found legal violations in 157. The board forwarded the 157 cases to the national police chief, who agreed with the findings in one case, partially accepted the findings in 27, and rejected the remainder. The IPCB's authority is limited to making recommendations to the NPH and reporting its findings to Parliament.13 The Parliamentary Commissioner for National and Ethnic Minority Rights (Minority Ombudsman) takes complaints from any person that feels that as a result of a government agency's decision, proceedings or negligence, a violation has taken place in her/his national or ethnic minority rights, or that the direct threat of such a violation is imminent. The documentary evidence indicates many other similar initiatives undertaken by the Hungarian government to address the problems of corruption within its police forces and to provide measures or avenues of complaint to the public.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds many police disciplinary actions and IPCB investigations, but police often reject IPCB recommendations; government has other initiatives.

propositions.text: Police still commit abuses against people including Roma, but authorities are reasonably expected to take action.
propositions.quote: The evidence indicates that police do still commit abuses against people, including the Roma, but there is also evidence that indicates it is reasonable to expect authorities to take action in these cases.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds police still abuse Roma but authorities are reasonably expected to act.

propositions.text: Claimant testified about rise in violent crime against Roma and investigation leading to charges for multiple murders and injuries.
propositions.quote: The claimant testified regarding the rise in violent crime against the Roma. On August 9, the National Bureau of Investigation announced the completion of its investigation into a series of physical attacks against Roma in 2008 and 2009.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified about violent crimes against Roma and related prosecutions.

propositions.text: Equal Treatment Authority provides direct redress for discrimination since 2005 with increasing complaints.
propositions.quote: There is also recourse to the Equal Treatment Authority. Since 2005 it has provided individuals with a direct avenue of redress for violations of the prohibition of discrimination in a variety of public and private law relationships.

propositions.text: Other remedies include courts and Parliamentary Commissioners; Roma Police Officers' Association accepts complaints mostly about discrimination.
propositions.quote: There are also other remedies such as seeking compensation through the courts, or turning to one of the Parliamentary Commissioners where public authorities are concerned. There is also the Roma Police Officers' Association in Hungary and Roma are able to file a complaint to the association.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker notes multiple remedies for Roma discrimination including Equal Treatment Authority and Roma Police Officers' Association.

propositions.text: Claimant has access to multiple programs for assistance if facing discrimination.
propositions.quote: If the claimant faces discrimination, he has recourse to all these programs for assistance should he need it.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant has access to programs for assistance against discrimination.

propositions.text: Hungarian government has taken legal and institutional measures to improve Roma situation, with advanced minority protection system.
propositions.quote: The Hungarian government has taken a number of legal and institutional measures to improve the situation of the Romani minority. According to the open Society Institute, Hungary has one of the most advanced systems for minority protection in the region.

propositions.text: Government institutions include Roma Integration Department and Council of Roma Integration coordinating social inclusion measures.
propositions.quote: The Hungarian Government lists a number of institutions within the state apparatus, including the Roma Integration Department within the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor, the main government body responsible for Romani integration and the Council of Roma Integration, a consultative, advisory body, which coordinates measures between various ministries on the social inclusion of Roma.

propositions.text: Hungary has initiatives in education, employment, housing, health, and political representation for Roma.
propositions.quote: Hungary has taken a number of initiatives relating to the situation of the Roma including, education, employment, housing, health, and political representation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Hungary has advanced minority protection and multiple initiatives for Roma inclusion.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows ministries and labor centers have special officers for Roma affairs and programs for integration and infrastructure.
propositions.quote: Most ministries and county labour affairs centers had special officers for Romani affairs focused on the needs of the Romani community. The Ministry of National Resources continued to offer financial incentives to encourage schools to integrate Romani and non-Romani children in the same classrooms and to reintegrate Roma inappropriately placed in remedial programs.

propositions.text: Ministry operates anti-discrimination legal aid network, though access and case acceptance issues exist.
propositions.quote: The Ministry of Public Administration and Justice (formerly the Ministry of Justice and Law Enforcement) operated an antidiscrimination legal service network that provided free legal aid to Roma in cases where they encountered ethnic discrimination. Human rights NGOs lamented that the lawyers' offices were located in the larger cities, rendering them inaccessible to those Roma living in deep poverty in small villages. HCLU received reports that the network's lawyers rejected some Romani cases.

propositions.text: Government requires desegregation plans for urban rehabilitation and education projects and opened public administration positions for Romani graduates.
propositions.quote: Since January 2009, in order to apply for EU and government funds for urban rehabilitation and public education projects, every city must attach to its proposal a desegregation plan outlining planned actions to eradicate segregation in housing and public education. The government opened 200 positions in public administration for Romani college graduates.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds ministries have Roma officers, legal aid networks, desegregation plans, and public administration jobs for Roma.

propositions.text: Hungary faces criticism for law enforcement implementation but is motivated and responsible as EU member to uphold standards.
propositions.quote: Hungary faces criticisms regarding the implementation of the laws that it has enacted to address the discrimination and persecution of its minorities, especially the Romani. While there may be motivation within the central government to have its laws enforced, there is difficulty in implementing the enforcement of these laws at the local level, and resources routinely fail to reach the groups with the greatest needs.

propositions.text: Hungary is monitored by European bodies like ECRI which praises accomplishments and recommends future action.
propositions.quote: The European Commission against Racism and Intolerance (ECRI) was established by the Council of Europe. It is an independent human rights monitoring body specialized in questions relating to racism and intolerance. It is composed of independent and impartial members, who are appointed on the basis of their moral authority and recognized expertise in dealing with racism, xenophobia, anti-Semitism and intolerance. The ECRI published a report on Hungary in which gives praise to Hungary for its accomplishments, cites issues of concern, and gives recommendation for future action.

propositions.text: Hungary is not isolated but a responsible EU member taking measures to implement mandated standards on racism.
propositions.quote: What is important to note in this instance, is that Hungary is not an island unto its own, but it is a responsible member of the European Union and reports regularly to the governance structures within that Union. Even if criticism of Hungary's measures to combat racism is warranted, particularly against the Romani population, on a balance of probabilities, Hungary is taking the measures to implement the standards that are mandated as a member of the European Union.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Hungary faces implementation criticism but is a responsible EU member taking mandated anti-racism measures.

propositions.text: Claimants failed to rebut presumption of state protection with clear and convincing evidence and did not take all reasonable steps to seek protection.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimants, in the circumstances of this case, have failed to rebut the presumption of state protection with clear and convincing evidence and that the claimants did not take all reasonable steps in the circumstances to avail themselves of that protection before making claims for refugee protection.

propositions.text: Not persuaded Hungary would not provide reasonable state protection if claimants sought it.
propositions.quote: Therefore, I am not persuaded that the state of Hungary would not be reasonably forthcoming with state protection, should the claimants seek it.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimants failed to rebut state protection presumption and Hungary would provide reasonable protection.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection as state protection is available.
propositions.quote: I find that that the claimant is not a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection, whether under section 96 or section 97 of the Act, as state protection is available to them.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimant is not a refugee or protected person as state protection is available.

propositions.text: Claims of claimant's family members joined to his claim also fail.
propositions.quote: Since the claims of the principal claimant's spouse, XXXXX XXXXX, and their minor children, XXXXX XXXXX and XXXXX XXXXX, their adult son XXXXX XXXXX (Jr.) and his common-law spouse, XXXXX XXXXX, and the claimant's spouse's father (claimant's father-in-law) XXXXX XXXXX, are joined to his claim, their claims too must fail.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claims of the claimant's family members also fail.

propositions.text: Court states it has applied certain principles and jurisprudence in this case.
propositions.quote: In the case at hand, I have applied the following principles and jurisprudence.

paragraphs.summary: The court states it applied principles and jurisprudence in this case.

propositions.text: Board guided by Supreme Court and Federal Court jurisprudence on state protection applied here.
propositions.quote: The Board, in assessing the issue of state protection, is guided by the jurisprudence from the Supreme Court of Canada and the Federal Court. The courts have established a number of principles relating to state protection and I have applied those principles to the case at hand.

paragraphs.summary: The court states it applied Supreme Court and Federal Court jurisprudence on state protection.

propositions.text: Presumption that state can protect citizens except when state is in complete breakdown.
propositions.quote: There is a presumption that, except in situations where the state is in complete breakdown, the state is capable of protecting its citizens.

propositions.text: International protection applies only when claimant has no other recourse; Hungary is in effective control with functioning security forces.
propositions.quote: The presumption that a state is capable of protecting its citizens underscores the principle that international protection comes into play only when a refugee claimant has no other recourse available. Having canvassed the country conditions documents, I find that Hungary is in effective control of its territory and has in place a functioning security force to uphold the laws and constitution of the country.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the presumption that states can protect citizens unless in breakdown; Hungary is in effective control.

propositions.text: Claimant must provide clear and convincing evidence to rebut presumption of state protection.
propositions.quote: To rebut the presumption of state protection, a claimant must provide "clear and convincing" confirmation of the state's inability to protect its citizens.

propositions.text: Evidence must be reliable, probative, and satisfy balance of probabilities that protection is inadequate.
propositions.quote: The evidence that state protection is inadequate must not only be reliable and probative, it must also satisfy the Board, on a balance of probabilities, that state protection is inadequate.

propositions.text: State efforts not always successful do not rebut presumption if state is in effective control and makes serious efforts.
propositions.quote: Where a state is in effective control of its territory, has military, police and civil authority in place and makes serious efforts to protect its citizens, the mere fact that the state's efforts are not always successful will not rebut the presumption of state protection.

propositions.text: Subjective reluctance or untested doubts do not rebut presumption of state protection in functioning democracy.
propositions.quote: A claimant cannot rebut the presumption of state protection in a functioning democracy by asserting only a subjective reluctance to engage the state. Doubting the effectiveness of the protection offered by the state when one has not really tested it does not rebut the existence of a presumption of state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the high evidentiary standard to rebut state protection presumption in a functioning democracy.

propositions.text: Refugee protection is surrogate, invoked only after unsuccessful state protection attempts.
propositions.quote: Refugee protection is meant to be a form of surrogate protection to be invoked only in those situations where the refugee claimant has unsuccessfully sought the protection of their home state.

propositions.text: Onus on claimant to seek state protection if reasonably forthcoming; failure to do so usually fatal to claim in functioning democracy.
propositions.quote: The onus is on the claimant to approach the state for protection in situations where state protection might be reasonably forthcoming. To qualify for refugee status, a claimant must satisfy the Board that he or she sought, but was unable to obtain, protection from their home state, or alternatively, that their home state, on an objective basis, could not be expected to provide protection. In the absence of a compelling explanation, a failure to pursue state protection opportunities within the home state will usually be fatal to a refugee claim, at least where the state is a functioning democracy with a willingness and the apparatus necessary to provide a measure of protection to its citizens.

paragraphs.summary: The court states refugee protection is surrogate and claimants must seek state protection first in functioning democracies.

propositions.text: Claimant's burden of proof increases with level of democracy; Hungary is a democracy with free elections and independent judiciary.
propositions.quote: A claimant's burden of proof is directly proportional to the level of democracy in the state in question: the more democratic the state's institutions, the more the claimant must have done to exhaust all courses of action open to them. The documentary evidence before the Board indicates that Hungary is a democracy, and there are free and fair elections. There is a relatively independent and impartial judiciary.

propositions.text: Claimant must show all reasonable steps taken to seek protection considering country context; local failures do not imply state failure unless part of broader pattern.
propositions.quote: Therefore, in countries such as Hungary, the claimant must do more than merely show that he or she went to see members of the police force and that those efforts were unsuccessful. A claimant must show that they have taken all reasonable steps in the circumstances to seek protection, taking into account the context of the country of origin, the steps taken and the claimant's interactions with the authorities. Local failures by authorities to provide protection do not mean that the state as a whole fails to protect its citizens, unless the failures form part of a broader pattern of the state's inability or refusal to provide protection.

propositions.text: No government guarantees perfect protection; less than perfect protection is insufficient to deny state protection in effective control states.
propositions.quote: No government is expected to guarantee perfect protection to all of its citizens at all times, and the fact that a state is not always successful in protecting its citizens, is not enough to justify a claim, especially where a state is in effective control of its territory, has military, police and civil authorities in place and is making serious efforts to protect its citizens. Less than perfect protection is not a basis to determine that a state is either unwilling or unable to offer reasonable protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains claimant's heavy burden in democracies like Hungary and that imperfect protection does not negate state protection.

propositions.text: Claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection; claim rejected.
propositions.quote: I determine that the claimants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection. The Refugee Protection Division therefore rejects their claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimants are not refugees or protected persons and rejects their claim.
